stages.name: Trade and the environment
stages.title: Trade and the environment
stages.sub: How rising world trade creates environmental costs, and why governments sometimes restrict trade because of them.

steps.q: World trade has grown hugely, with far more goods shipped across oceans and far more factories running to supply them. Does moving and making all these extra goods use up more fuel and raw materials, or about the same as before?
steps.hint: Think about thousands more container ships sailing and factories running than before trade grew.

steps.q: All those extra ships burning fuel and factories running flat out to supply world trade - what happens to pollution, resource use and carbon emissions as a result?
steps.hint: More fuel burned and more materials dug up and used - what does that do to emissions and waste?

steps.q: A country specialises in one good and trades for the rest, so it produces far more of that good and ships it worldwide. Compared with making a little of everything just for itself, does this extra production and transport add environmental damage, or avoid it?
steps.hint: Specialising means producing more of one thing at scale and moving it further - what does that do to pollution and emissions?

steps.q: A government is worried about the pollution and resource damage caused by importing cheaply produced goods. Would blocking or taxing those imports help it protect the environment, or would it have no effect on environmental damage?
steps.right: It could help protect the environment
steps.wrong: It would have no effect on environmental damage
steps.hint: If imports are driving the pollution, what could limiting them do to that pollution?
